newsitem.title: JAPAN: NTT says to cut work force to 165,400 by March '98.
newsitem.headline: NTT says to cut work force to 165,400 by March '98.

text.p: Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) said on Friday that it plans to cut its work force to 165,400 by the end of March 1998 from an estimated 183,400 at the end of March 1997.
The cut in the work force at NTT's parent company will be largely made through a shift of 17,000 workers to one of its subsidiaries, an NTT official told a news conference.
He also said that personnel costs at NTT's parent company in the year to March 31, 1998, would be 1.81 trillion yen, down 46 billion yen from its estimated personnel costs for 1996/97.
But overall costs at parent NTT are expected to grow by 110 billion yen in 1997/98 from this year due to higher operating costs in other areas, he said.
NTT expects sales of ISDN digital lines, used for fast communications, for example through computers, to increase by more than 80 billion yen in 1997/98 from this year, he said.
But sales from conventional fixed telephone lines are expected to fall by 54 billion yen in 1997/98 from this year, partly due to a rate cut this month, he said.
NTT plans investment related to overseas business at 100 billion yen in 1997/98, another NTT official said at a separate news conference on Friday.
